messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: High error rate (5xx) on /v1/embeddings for customer acmeco — started ~09:40 UTC. Paging on-call.
Alice V: saw this on the embeddings dashboard, spike from ~09:39. 5xxs are ~25% of requests in eu-west-1.
Ben R: looking at logs now — a bunch of: `error: handler received chat payload on embeddings runtime -> unsupported input type` and then OOM-ish traces downstream.
Caroline M: that sounds like an interface mismatch. Did the routing policy pick a chat variant by accident?
Ben R: query mapping table: `select * from route_aliases where customer='acmeco'` returns alias anchored_version = "v2026-03-chat-anchored" for route embeddings
Alice V: wtf. How did an embeddings route get an anchor to a chat build? This will definitely return incompatible schema and trigger 500s.
oncall-jen: I'm on it. Paging SRE to coordinate mitigations. Marking severity P1 for customer-facing error rate.
SRE Pager: acknowledged. Initial plan: 1) temporary policy suspend for acmeco embeddings routing 2) re-route to compatible embeddings model 3) rollback anchor mapping 4) postmortem and customer comms.
oncall-jen: executing suspend now: `/routing suspend --customer acmeco --route embeddings --reason "incompatible-version-anchored"`
infra-deploy-bot: command accepted. Routing suspend job queued -> job id 6421. Expected propagation ~30s.
Ben R: while that runs, dumping recent alias-change audit: `grep acmeco /var/log/config-changes | tail -n 20` shows an automated alias sync at 09:34 that set anchored_version="v2026-03-chat-anchored" for multiple aliases after an internal rollout.
Caroline M: timeline suggests an automated alias sync mis-tagged several customers with the chat anchor when sync script matched on partial model name. root cause candidate: greedy regex in alias-sync.
Alice V: confirm suspend succeeded? We should watch the 5xx rate now.
infra-deploy-bot: job 6421 completed -> routing suspend applied. All new requests for acmeco embeddings will skip alias anchoring and use fallback routing policy.
oncall-jen: traffic is already dropping in 5xxs — down from 25% to ~1.8% in eu-west within one minute.
SRE Pager: great. Next step: set explicit alias to a compatible embeddings variant so we don't rely on fallback. Suggest embeddings-v2-quant.
Ben R: setting alias: `redwood alias set --customer acmeco --route embeddings --target embeddings-v2-quant --note "emergency fix"`
infra-deploy-bot: alias update accepted. Propagating to routing plane.
Caroline M: checking logs — new requests now show model=embeddings-v2-quant and successful responses. Error rate back to normal baseline.
CS Lead Mark: I just messaged the AcmeCo CSM and engineering contact, told them we are mitigating and will follow up with RCA and ETA for a permanent fix. They reported user-visible failures for ~7 minutes.
Alice V: quick ask: did the automated sync have a change window that overlapped a deployment? Might be why it picked chat anchor.
Ben R: yes, sync ran after a model rollout where chat variants had new naming. The regex matched `-anchored` suffix across model families.
oncall-jen: immediate mitigation done. Moving to containment -> remediation. Creating a patch to alias-sync to require explicit interface tag match (embedding|chat|gen) before applying.
SRE Pager: open action item: GH#1257 — add interface gating to alias-sync. Owner: Caroline. ETA: today EOD for PR, tomorrow for rollout.
Caroline M: noted, I'll push a branch and add unit tests that simulate mixed-name model catalogs.
Alice V: can we add a sanity check to routing plane: validate model interface compatibility before binding alias. If mismatch, fail the alias update and alert.
Ben R: good idea. I'll raise a follow-up ticket for the runtime check — GH#1258. Owner: Ben. ETA: 72h.
SRE Pager: post-incident ops: update runbook to include `routing suspend` as first step for interface-mismatch errors. Also add a quick query snippet for `unsupported input type` errors.
oncall-jen: handoff to next on-call in 20m — I'll keep an eye until then. Anyone want to add notes for timeline?
Alice V: timeline: 09:34 config sync mistakenly set chat anchor; 09:39 customer error spike begins; 09:40 incident-bot page; 09:42 suspend applied; 09:43 alias set to embeddings-v2-quant; 09:44 errors resolved. Customer impact ~7-10 minutes.
CS Lead Mark: AcmeCo reported elevated error rate and failed batch jobs. They will need detail for SLO forgiveness and postmortem. I'll send an initial status update: impact period and mitigation steps.
Caroline M: follow-ups: fix alias-sync regex (GH#1257), runtime interface validation (GH#1258), add pre-merge test harness that fakes catalog with mixed families (owner: QA, ETA 1 week), and retroactive scan to find other customers with recent alias changes same pattern (owner: Ben, ETA: 24h).
infra-deploy-bot: note: no infra-level rollback required; actions were config changes only.
oncall-jen: closing the P1 escalation now; keeping thread open for postmortem notes and action verification.
SRE Pager: please tag PRs with `incident-1779991234` so we can track. I'll draft a short incident summary for the ops channel.
Alice V: small addendum — we should also add a pre-deploy checklist item for catalog rollouts to avoid ambiguous names.
Caroline M: will include that in GH#1257.
CS Lead Mark: I'll coordinate customer follow-up: detailed timeline, mitigation, and ETA for permanent fix. Also double-check whether they saw data corruption (they did not; only failed requests).
Ben R: running one-off audit: `select customer, alias, anchored_version from route_aliases where anchored_version like '%-chat-%' and updated_at > now() - interval '2 days'` to find other potentially impacted customers.
oncall-jen: thanks team. handing off to Ben for audits and Caroline for PR. I'll be reachable if anything re-escalates. :thumbsup:
SRE Pager: Incident resolved for now. Postmortem owners assigned: Caroline (root cause + PR), Ben (audit + runtime check ticket), Mark (customer comms). Close this thread when GHs are linked.
